title: Group Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: NAB People
tiers.description: Each director, officer, employee, secondee and contract-hire of NAB or a Group member. Bound by the insider trading ban, the short-term/speculative ban (short selling, stock lending, 30-day hold), the bi-annual Black-out Periods, ad hoc restrictions and the Derivatives and Hedging rules; no Compliance Certificate unless also a Director or Designated NAB Employee.

tiers.name: Designated NAB Employees
tiers.description: Office of the Group CEO, Executive Leadership Team members and their direct reports, BNZ directors/executives/company secretaries, EGM Audit and reports, Disclosure Committee, Group Treasury capital/funding staff, Investor Relations, Corporate Affairs (external), Group Development, Corporate Advisory Legal, Capital & Funding Legal, Group Governance, designated Finance/Data/Economics staff and anyone designated in writing by the Group Company Secretary. Must lodge a Compliance Certificate before Trading, DRP/SPP elections and Derivative transactions.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Directors of National Australia Bank Limited (including the Group CEO). Compliance Certificate to the Chair then Group Company Secretary before Trades, Derivative transactions and Margin Loans; ASX notification of Notifiable Interests within 1 business day; case-by-case Derivative approval from the Chair.

tiers.name: Executive Leadership Team
tiers.description: Senior executives reporting directly to the Group CEO. Designated NAB Employees who must additionally lodge a Compliance Certificate before entering a Margin Loan or adding Group Securities as security; must inform the Group Company Secretary of margin-call risk; Derivative approval from the Group CEO or delegate.

tiers.name: Key Management Personnel
tiers.description: KMP under Australian Accounting Standards, currently Directors and the Executive Leadership Team. They and their Closely Related Parties must not use Derivatives or Hedging Arrangements over remuneration that is unvested or vested but subject to forfeiture conditions; NAB publicly discloses all their Derivative positions.

tiers.name: Immediate Family Members and controlled entities
tiers.description: Partner, children, partner's children and dependants of a NAB Person, and companies, trusts and entities controlled by them. Bound by the Black-out Periods; Directors and Designated NAB Employees must lodge a Compliance Certificate and prevent a proposed Trade by them until acknowledged.

definitions.hedging_definition: An arrangement that would have the effect of limiting exposure to risk and includes, but is not limited to, arrangements referred to in Corporations Regulation 2D.7.01(1). Arrangements referred to in Corporations Regulation 2D.7.01(2) are excluded.

10.00am AEST on the ASX trading day after the day NAB's full-year results are released

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: NAB may impose ad hoc restrictions on Trading in Group Securities when there is a heightened risk of NAB People having Inside Information (e.g. a planned transaction), on all NAB People or individually identified employees. No specific officer is named and confidentiality is not addressed.

rules.detail: Absolute ban on Derivatives (s761D, expressly including options, forwards, swaps, caps and collars) over unvested Group Securities for all NAB People. Vested means NAB-imposed time and performance hurdles satisfied, ignoring any longer restriction the person elected.
rules.evidence: Accordingly, all NAB People are prohibited from using Derivatives or otherwise entering into Hedging Arrangements in relation to any unvested Group Securities.

rules.detail: KMP (Directors and ELT) and their Closely Related Parties may not use Derivatives over remuneration elements that have vested but remain subject to forfeiture (clawback/malus) conditions.
rules.evidence: Key Management Personnel and their Closely Related Parties must not use Derivatives or otherwise enter into Hedging Arrangements in relation to elements of their remuneration that are unvested or which have vested but remain subject to forfeiture conditions.

rules.detail: Derivatives over vested Group Securities are allowed only (a) to protect an asset supporting a loan for the exercise price of NAB options, (b) to protect value where a tax liability is payable at the tax cessation time, or (c) case-by-case with approval from the Chair (Directors), Group Company Secretary (Chair) or Group CEO or delegate (ELT and all other NAB People). Every Derivative must mature within the eight-week period immediately following release of half-year or full-year results, and no Group member may be counterparty. Directors and Designated NAB Employees must also lodge a Compliance Certificate. Venue is unrestricted, so an OTC collar with an external bank qualifies.
rules.evidence: once Group Securities have vested (as described above), Derivatives may be used by NAB People in relation to those vested securities in the following circumstances: ... on a case-by-case basis with approval from either the Chair in relation to Directors, the Group Company Secretary in relation to the Chair or the Group Chief Executive Officer or delegate in relation to Executive Leadership Team members and all other NAB People.

rules.detail: Hedging Arrangements (any arrangement limiting exposure to risk, including Corporations Regulation 2D.7.01(1) arrangements) over unvested Group Securities are banned for all NAB People; the policy notes it is also unlawful for KMP.
rules.evidence: all NAB People are prohibited from using Derivatives or otherwise entering into Hedging Arrangements in relation to any unvested Group Securities.

rules.detail: Extends the hedging ban for KMP and Closely Related Parties to vested remuneration still subject to forfeiture conditions.
rules.evidence: must not use Derivatives or otherwise enter into Hedging Arrangements in relation to elements of their remuneration that are unvested or which have vested but remain subject to forfeiture conditions.

rules.detail: Protective (value-protecting) use of Derivatives over vested securities is expressly contemplated as encouraging long-term holding, subject to the three permitted circumstances, the eight-week post-results maturity rule, no Group counterparty and the Compliance Certificate process.
rules.evidence: If the NAB-imposed time and performance hurdles applicable to Group Securities have been satisfied ... then the appropriate use of Derivatives can encourage longer term holding of Group Securities by NAB People.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward or similar is a Derivative (forward contract) and so is subject to the Derivatives regime (banned over unvested, restricted purposes and maturity over vested); any loan secured on Group Securities is a Margin Loan requiring a Compliance Certificate from Directors and ELT.
rules.evidence: Derivatives: Has the meaning given in s761D of the Corporations Act and includes options, forward contracts, futures, warrants, swaps, caps and collars

rules.detail: Outright ban on arrangements for short selling Group Securities, framed as part of the speculative trading prohibition.
rules.evidence: a NAB Person must not enter into any arrangements for short selling or stock lending in relation to Group Securities

rules.detail: Outright ban on stock lending arrangements over Group Securities. Note the Margin Loan definition separately treats securities 'lent' to a financier as a Margin Loan.
rules.evidence: a NAB Person must not enter into any arrangements for short selling or stock lending in relation to Group Securities

rules.detail: CFDs are not named but are s761D Derivatives, so are banned over unvested securities and over vested securities are confined to the three permitted purposes with the eight-week maturity rule; a speculative CFD would also breach the short-term gain ban and a short CFD the short-selling ban.
rules.evidence: A NAB Person must not deal in Group Securities for short-term gain.

rules.detail: Directors must lodge a Compliance Certificate before entering a Margin Loan (any loan where NAB Securities are mortgaged, provided as security, lent or charged to a financier) or agreeing to provide additional Group Securities as security for an existing one, and must inform the Group Company Secretary if a financier's demand may force disposal of Group Securities.
rules.evidence: Directors and Executive Leadership Team members (but not other Designated NAB Employees) must submit a Compliance Certificate before they enter into a Margin Loan or agree to provide additional Group Securities as security for an existing Margin Loan.

rules.detail: Same Compliance Certificate gate before entering a Margin Loan or topping up security, plus the margin-call risk notification to the Group Company Secretary.
rules.evidence: Directors and Executive Leadership Team members (but not other Designated NAB Employees) must submit a Compliance Certificate before they enter into a Margin Loan or agree to provide additional Group Securities as security for an existing Margin Loan.

rules.detail: Margin Loans are not prohibited for NAB People generally, and other Designated NAB Employees are expressly excluded from the Compliance Certificate requirement for Margin Loans. Any lender-forced sale would still be a Trade subject to Black-out Periods and the insider trading ban.
rules.evidence: Directors and Executive Leadership Team members (but not other Designated NAB Employees) must submit a Compliance Certificate before they enter into a Margin Loan

rules.detail: Mortgaging, charging or providing NAB Securities as security to a financier is by definition a Margin Loan, so Directors need a Compliance Certificate before granting or adding security. An encumbrance in favour of a non-financier is not addressed and is not a Trade.
rules.evidence: Margin Loan: A loan arrangement whereby NAB Securities are mortgaged, provided as security, lent, or charged to a financier.

rules.detail: As for Directors: granting or adding security over Group Securities to a financier requires a prior Compliance Certificate.
rules.evidence: Margin Loan: A loan arrangement whereby NAB Securities are mortgaged, provided as security, lent, or charged to a financier.

rules.detail: No restriction on other NAB People granting security over Group Securities; the Compliance Certificate requirement for Margin Loans is expressly confined to Directors and ELT.
rules.evidence: Directors and Executive Leadership Team members (but not other Designated NAB Employees) must submit a Compliance Certificate before they enter into a Margin Loan

rules.detail: The Margin Loan definition captures any loan arrangement secured on NAB Securities, not just broker margin facilities, so the loan leg of a funded collar is a Margin Loan: Compliance Certificate before inception and before any collateral top-up, and margin-call risk reporting to the Group Company Secretary for disclosure assessment. No outright prohibition and no vesting-state carve-out.
rules.evidence: Directors and members of the Executive Leadership Team are required to inform the Group Company Secretary where a financier demands payment under a Margin Loan and there is a risk that the demand will not be able to be satisfied without the disposal of Group Securities.

rules.detail: Same as Directors: any loan secured on Group Securities is a Margin Loan requiring a prior Compliance Certificate and margin-call risk reporting.
rules.evidence: must submit a Compliance Certificate before they enter into a Margin Loan or agree to provide additional Group Securities as security for an existing Margin Loan.

rules.detail: Secured financing over Group Securities is not restricted for NAB People below Directors and ELT.
rules.evidence: (but not other Designated NAB Employees)

rules.detail: No dealing in Group Securities for short-term gain; every acquisition triggers a 30-day period in which that type of Group Security cannot be sold. Vesting/exercise of performance rights and sale of the resulting shares within 30 days are carved out.
rules.evidence: any acquisition of Group Securities by a NAB Person triggers a 30 day period where that type of Group Securities cannot be sold.

exemption_authority: In Exceptional Circumstances (severe financial hardship requiring a sale, or a court order or legal/regulatory requirement to sell) the Board delegates written exemptions from the Policy to the Chair, Group CEO or delegate, Group CFO or delegate, Group Executive Legal & Commercial Services or delegate, or Group Company Secretary or delegate, at their discretion; an exemption is valid 5 business days and still requires a Compliance Certificate. Separately, the Group Executive Legal & Commercial Services or delegate may exempt a person from the Compliance Certificate requirement. Section 5.1 states there are no exceptions to the Policy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the Derivative must have a maturity date that falls within the eight-week period that immediately follows the date on which either NAB's half-year or full-year financial results are released to the ASX
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The collar's put and call must both expire within eight weeks after a results release, which fixes the available tenors (roughly six or twelve months from an open window) and rules out long-dated or open-ended structures.

bespoke_clauses.clause: neither NAB nor any member of the Group can be a counterparty to the Derivative.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The collar and, prudently, the loan must be written by a bank outside the NAB Group; NAB's own markets desk cannot face the executive.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Derivatives may be used by NAB People in relation to those vested securities in the following circumstances: to protect the value of an asset supporting a loan taken out for the exercise price of options granted by NAB; to protect the value of the Group Security where the employee has paid or is required to pay a tax liability at the tax cessation time; or on a case-by-case basis with approval
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A general funded collar falls outside the two self-executing purposes and needs discretionary case-by-case approval (Chair for Directors, Group Company Secretary for the Chair, Group CEO or delegate for ELT and others) in addition to the Compliance Certificate.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Group Securities are considered vested once the NAB-imposed time and performance hurdles have been satisfied, irrespective of whether a NAB Person has opted for a longer period of restriction
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Shares under a voluntary extended holding lock are collar-eligible, but for KMP shares that remain subject to forfeiture conditions after vesting are still off limits under 3.5.5.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Margin Loan: A loan arrangement whereby NAB Securities are mortgaged, provided as security, lent, or charged to a financier.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank loan secured on the collared shares is a Margin Loan regardless of label, so Directors and ELT must lodge a Compliance Certificate before drawdown and before any collateral top-up.

bespoke_clauses.clause: NAB will publicly disclose all Derivative positions over Group Securities taken out by a Director or by Key Management Personnel of the Group ... irrespective of whether or not the particular form of Derivative technically falls within the disclosure requirements of the ASX Listing Rules or the Corporations Act.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A Director's or ELT member's collar will be announced to the market and reported in the Annual Financial Report even if it would not otherwise be notifiable, so confidentiality of the structure cannot be assumed.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and members of the Executive Leadership Team are required to inform the Group Company Secretary where a financier demands payment under a Margin Loan and there is a risk that the demand will not be able to be satisfied without the disposal of Group Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any loan-to-value breach or margin call on the funded collar may have to be escalated internally and potentially disclosed to the market; the policy is silent on whether a forced sale in a Black-out Period is a breach.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Acknowledgment of the Compliance Certificate by NAB is intended as a compliance monitoring function only, and is not an endorsement of the proposed transaction.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The certificate is a no-inside-information confirmation acknowledged by the Chair or manager rather than a substantive approval, and the Trade must occur within 5 business days of acknowledgement.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Performance rights must only be exercised outside the Black-out Periods.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Shares to be collared must be settled from exercise outside the roughly six-week Black-out Periods beginning 16 March and 16 September, and the collar itself as a Trade in Derivatives is likewise confined to open periods.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Must not: Means an action is explicitly prohibited and any deviation from this will require a formal policy exemption.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Written exemptions are available only in Exceptional Circumstances (hardship or legal compulsion to sell), so they cannot be used to permit a collar over unvested or forfeitable securities.

summary: A funded collar is possible for NAB Directors and Executive Leadership Team members, but only over Group Securities whose NAB-imposed time and performance hurdles have been satisfied and, for KMP, that are no longer subject to forfeiture conditions; derivatives and hedging over unvested securities are banned outright. Because a general collar is not one of the two self-executing permitted purposes, it requires case-by-case approval (Chair for Directors, Group Company Secretary for the Chair, Group CEO or delegate for ELT), and both legs must mature within the eight-week period after a half-year or full-year results release and be written by a counterparty outside the NAB Group. The loan secured on the collared shares is a Margin Loan under the policy's broad definition, so Directors and ELT must lodge a Compliance Certificate before entering it and before any collateral top-up, and must report to the Group Company Secretary if a margin demand may force a sale. The derivative itself needs a Compliance Certificate, execution within 5 business days of acknowledgement, and must fall outside the 16 March and 16 September Black-out Periods and any ad hoc restriction; NAB will publicly disclose all Director and KMP derivative positions. Written exemptions exist only for hardship or court-ordered sales.
